# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run a LAMMPS ReaxFF simulation
# on a single ARM-based AWS node within a Kubernetes cluster using the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Using an incrementing name to avoid collisions during repeated tests.
  name: lammps-reax-minicluster-1
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # tasks is intentionally omitted. Flux will automatically size the job
  # to use all available CPU cores on the single node.

  # Logging mode is set to strict to ensure all output is captured.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # This job is for testing; pods are not cleaned up upon completion
  # to allow for log inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

  flux:
    # Specify the architecture as ARM for AWS ARM-based instances.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Disabling the separate Flux sidecar container.
      # This modern approach assumes the `flux` executable is present in the main application container.
      disable: true

  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to execute the LAMMPS simulation.
      # The Flux Operator will prepend `flux run -n <tasks> ...` to this command.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # The launcher flag must be false for the main application container.
      launcher: false

      # Ensure the latest version of the container is always pulled for the experiment.
      imagePullPolicy: Always

      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).
      # This is necessary for high-performance networking on supported AWS instances.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest addresses an ImagePullBackOff failure
# by explicitly setting the ARM-compatible Flux container image.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Using an incrementing name to avoid collisions with the previous failed attempt.
  name: lammps-reax-minicluster-2
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # tasks is intentionally omitted. Flux will automatically size the job
  # to use all available CPU cores on the single node.

  # Logging mode is set to strict to ensure all output is captured.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # This job is for testing; pods are not cleaned up upon completion
  # to allow for log inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

  flux:
    # Specify the architecture as ARM for AWS Graviton (ARM-based) instances.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # This setting tells the operator not to inject the Flux sidecar container,
      # as the main container is expected to have Flux binaries.
      disable: true
      # FIX: Despite disabling the container, the operator was attempting to resolve an image.
      # This explicitly sets the correct ARM-compatible image to prevent the ImagePullBackOff error.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy

  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to execute the LAMMPS simulation.
      # The Flux Operator will prepend `flux run` to this command.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # The launcher flag must be false for the main application container.
      launcher: false

      # Ensure the latest version of the container is always pulled for the experiment.
      imagePullPolicy: Always

      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).
      # This is necessary for high-performance networking on supported AWS instances.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
